title: Discovery of Ceres
desc: Giuseppe Piazzi discovered Ceres, the first asteroid to be identified, located between Mars and Jupiter.

title: Emancipation Proclamation
desc: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation took effect, declaring freedom for slaves in Confederate states.

title: Internet's first .com
desc: Symbolics.com was registered, becoming the first commercial .com domain name on the internet.

title: Euro introduced
desc: The euro was officially introduced as the single currency for 11 EU member states, initially in electronic form.

title: Euro notes & coins
desc: Euro banknotes and coins entered circulation across 12 European countries, the largest cash changeover in history.

title: Bitcoin genesis block
desc: Satoshi Nakamoto mined the Bitcoin genesis block (Block 0), launching the world's first decentralized cryptocurrency.

title: Birth of Louis Braille
desc: Louis Braille, inventor of the Braille reading and writing system for the blind, was born in Coupvray, France.

title: Construction of Golden Gate Bridge
desc: Construction began on the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco, then the longest suspension bridge in the world.

title: Galileo discovers Jupiter's moons
desc: Galileo Galilei observed Jupiter's four largest moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto), proving not all bodies orbit Earth.

title: First channel crossing by air
desc: French inventor Jean-Pierre Blanchard and American John Jeffries crossed the English Channel in a hydrogen balloon.

title: First transatlantic phone call
desc: The first commercial transatlantic telephone call was made between New York and London via radio telephone.

title: Death of Nikola Tesla
desc: Serbian-American inventor Nikola Tesla died in a New York hotel room, aged 86, penniless but legendary.

title: Death of Galileo Galilei
desc: Italian astronomer and physicist Galileo Galilei died in Arcetri, Italy, aged 77, after a lifetime of pioneering astronomical discoveries.

title: Birth of Elvis Presley
desc: Elvis Aaron Presley, the 'King of Rock and Roll', was born in Tupelo, Mississippi, USA.

title: Birth of Stephen Hawking
desc: British theoretical physicist and cosmologist Stephen Hawking was born in Oxford, England.

title: Death of Marco Polo
desc: Venetian merchant and explorer Marco Polo, who traveled the Silk Road to China, died in Venice.

title: Steve Jobs unveils iPhone
desc: Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone at MacWorld in San Francisco, revolutionizing mobile phones forever.

title: First section of London Underground
desc: The Metropolitan Railway, the world's first underground railway, opened in London between Paddington and Farringdon.

title: Death of David Bowie
desc: British rock legend David Bowie died in New York two days after releasing his final album 'Blackstar'.

title: Birth of William James
desc: American philosopher and psychologist William James, the 'Father of American psychology', was born in New York.

title: Death of Whitney Houston
desc: American singer and actress Whitney Houston died in Beverly Hills, California, aged 48.

title: 2010 Haiti earthquake
desc: A catastrophic 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck Haiti, killing over 200,000 people and devastating the capital Port-au-Prince.

title: US ratifies Treaty of Paris
desc: The United States Congress ratified the Treaty of Paris, officially ending the American Revolutionary War with Great Britain.

title: Coronation of Elizabeth I
desc: Elizabeth I was crowned Queen of England in Westminster Abbey, beginning a 45-year reign known as the Elizabethan era.

title: Birth of Martin Luther King Jr.
desc: American civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia.

title: Wikipedia launched
desc: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia, the free online encyclopedia that anyone can edit.

title: Death of Ivan the Terrible
desc: Ivan IV ('the Terrible'), the first Tsar of Russia, died in Moscow, ending a 37-year reign of terror and expansion.

title: First operational laser
desc: Theodore Maiman demonstrated the first working laser (a ruby laser) at Hughes Research Laboratories in California.

title: Overthrow of Hawaiian monarchy
desc: U.S. Marines and American settlers overthrew Queen Liliuokalani of Hawaii, leading to eventual U.S. annexation.

title: Northridge earthquake
desc: A 6.7 earthquake struck the San Fernando Valley near Los Angeles, killing 57 and causing $20B in damage.

title: Birth of Edgar Allan Poe
desc: American writer and poet Edgar Allan Poe, master of the macabre, was born in Boston, Massachusetts.

title: First English Parliament
desc: The first elected English Parliament, summoned by Simon de Montfort, convened in Westminster.

title: First FIFA World Cup match
desc: The first-ever FIFA World Cup match was played in Montevideo, Uruguay, with France defeating Mexico 4-1.

title: Execution of Louis XVI
desc: King Louis XVI of France was guillotined in Paris's Place de la Revolution, during the French Revolution.

title: Death of Queen Victoria
desc: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom died at Osborne House after a 63-year reign, the longest in British history at that time.

title: Bloody Sunday, Russia
desc: Tsarist troops fired on a peaceful workers' procession in St. Petersburg, killing hundreds and sparking the 1905 Russian Revolution.

title: Shaanxi earthquake
desc: The deadliest earthquake in recorded history struck Shaanxi, China, killing an estimated 830,000 people.

title: California Gold Rush
desc: James W. Marshall discovered gold at Sutter's Mill in Coloma, California, sparking the California Gold Rush.

title: Birth of Robert Burns
desc: Scottish poet Robert Burns, widely regarded as the national poet of Scotland, was born in Alloway.

title: Birth of Mozart
desc: Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of the greatest composers in history, was born in Salzburg.

title: Birth of Lewis Carroll
desc: English writer and mathematician Lewis Carroll, author of 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland', was born in Cheshire.

title: 'Pride and Prejudice' published
desc: Jane Austen's novel 'Pride and Prejudice' was published in the United Kingdom, becoming a literary classic.

title: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
desc: Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff, killing all seven crew members including teacher Christa McAuliffe.

title: Death of Gandhi
desc: Mahatma Gandhi, leader of India's independence movement, was assassinated in New Delhi by a Hindu nationalist.

title: Execution of Guy Fawkes
desc: Guy Fawkes was executed in London for his role in the Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament in 1605.

title: Columbia disaster
desc: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during re-entry, killing all seven astronauts aboard, including Israel's first astronaut Ilan Ramon.

title: The Day the Music Died
desc: Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and J.P. 'The Big Bopper' Richardson died in a plane crash near Clear Lake, Iowa.

title: Patty Hearst kidnapped
desc: Newspaper heiress Patty Hearst was kidnapped by the Symbionese Liberation Army in Berkeley, California.

title: Facebook founded
desc: Mark Zuckerberg launched 'TheFacebook' from his Harvard dormitory, the beginning of the world's largest social network.

title: Birth of Cristiano Ronaldo
desc: Portuguese football star Cristiano Ronaldo was born in Funchal, Madeira, Portugal.

title: Death of King George VI
desc: King George VI of the United Kingdom died, and his daughter Elizabeth II ascended to the throne.

title: Munich air disaster
desc: A plane carrying the Manchester United football team crashed in Munich, killing 23 people including eight players.

title: Birth of Charles Dickens
desc: English novelist Charles Dickens, author of 'A Tale of Two Cities' and 'Oliver Twist', was born in Portsmouth, England.

title: Execution of Mary, Queen of Scots
desc: Mary, Queen of Scots was executed at Fotheringhay Castle on orders of Queen Elizabeth I of England.

title: Birth of Jules Verne
desc: French novelist Jules Verne, pioneer of science fiction, was born in Nantes, France.

title: Davis Cup founded
desc: The Davis Cup tennis tournament was established when the United States played Great Britain in Boston.

title: Deep Blue defeats Kasparov
desc: IBM's chess computer Deep Blue became the first machine to win a chess game against a reigning world champion (Garry Kasparov).

title: Birth of Thomas Edison
desc: American inventor Thomas Alva Edison, holder of over 1,000 patents including the phonograph and practical light bulb, was born in Milan, Ohio.

title: Lateran Treaty signed
desc: The Lateran Treaty created the independent State of Vatican City, resolving the 'Roman Question' with Italy.

title: Mandela released
desc: Nelson Mandela was released from Victor Verster Prison after 27 years, accelerating the end of apartheid.

title: Birth of Charles Darwin
desc: English naturalist Charles Darwin, who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, was born in Shrewsbury.

title: Birth of Abraham Lincoln
desc: Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States, was born in Hodgenville, Kentucky.

title: Discovery of transposons
desc: Barbara McClintock discovered 'jumping genes' (transposons) in maize, later winning the Nobel Prize for the work.

title: Galileo on trial
desc: Galileo Galilei arrived in Rome to face trial by the Inquisition for supporting the heliocentric model of the solar system.

title: Oregon becomes a state
desc: Oregon was admitted as the 33rd state of the United States of America.

title: Bell patents telephone
desc: Alexander Graham Bell filed the patent for the telephone, beating Elisha Gray's similar filing by only hours.

title: St. Valentine's Day Massacre
desc: Seven members of Chicago's North Side Gang were murdered by Al Capone's men in a Prohibition-era gang hit.

title: YouTube launched
desc: Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim registered youtube.com, which went on to become the world's largest video platform.

title: Birth of Galileo Galilei
desc: Italian astronomer, physicist and 'father of modern science' Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa.

title: Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
desc: The Soviet Union officially completed its military withdrawal from Afghanistan after a 10-year war.

title: Opening of Tutankhamun's tomb
desc: Howard Carter's team opened the sealed doorway to the burial chamber of Pharaoh Tutankhamun in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.

title: Giordano Bruno burned
desc: Italian philosopher Giordano Bruno was burned at the stake in Rome for heresy, including his belief in an infinite universe.

title: Death of Michelangelo
desc: Italian Renaissance sculptor and painter Michelangelo died in Rome, aged 88.

title: Birth of Copernicus
desc: Polish astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, who proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system, was born in Torun.

title: First American orbits Earth
desc: Astronaut John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth aboard Friendship 7, completing three orbits.

title: Assassination of Malcolm X
desc: African-American activist Malcolm X was assassinated in New York City while preparing to address his organization.

title: Death of Amerigo Vespucci
desc: Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci, who gave his name to the Americas, died in Seville, Spain.

title: Birth of George Washington
desc: George Washington, the first President of the United States and commander of the Continental Army, was born in Virginia.

title: Gutenberg Bible printed
desc: Johannes Gutenberg completed the first major book printed with movable type in Mainz, Germany, launching the printing revolution.

title: Birth of Steve Jobs
desc: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs was born in San Francisco, California.

title: Colt revolver patented
desc: American inventor Samuel Colt received a U.S. patent for his revolving-cylinder pistol, the first practical repeating firearm.

title: First Volkswagen Beetle
desc: Adolf Hitler laid the foundation stone for the first Volkswagen factory, with Ferdinand Porsche designing the 'people's car'.

title: DNA double helix discovered
desc: James Watson and Francis Crick announced their discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA at Cambridge.

title: Hattie McDaniel wins Oscar
desc: Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award for her role in 'Gone with the Wind'.

title: Birth of Chopin
desc: Polish composer and piano virtuoso Frederic Chopin was born in Zelazowa Wola, Poland.

title: Concorde first flight
desc: The Anglo-French supersonic airliner Concorde made its maiden flight from Toulouse, France.

title: Birth of Alexander Graham Bell
desc: Scottish-born inventor Alexander Graham Bell, credited with inventing the first practical telephone, was born in Edinburgh.

title: Copernican book banned
desc: The Catholic Church placed Copernicus' 'De Revolutionibus' on its Index of Forbidden Books pending 'correction'.

title: Kepler's third law
desc: Johannes Kepler discovered his third law of planetary motion, describing the relationship between orbital period and distance.

title: Birth of Karl Marx
desc: German philosopher and economist Karl Marx, founder of modern communism, was born in Trier, Prussia.

title: Death of Stalin
desc: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died in Moscow, ending nearly 30 years of brutal rule over the Soviet Union.

title: Birth of Michelangelo
desc: Italian Renaissance sculptor, painter, and architect Michelangelo Buonarroti was born in Caprese, Tuscany.

title: Birth of Ravel
desc: French composer Maurice Ravel, known for 'Bolero', was born in Ciboure, France.

title: Bell patents telephone
desc: Alexander Graham Bell was granted U.S. Patent 174,465 for the telephone, one of history's most valuable patents.

title: Birth of Amerigo Vespucci
desc: Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci, from whose name 'America' is derived, was born in Florence.

title: First telephone call
desc: Alexander Graham Bell made the first successful telephone call to his assistant: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'

title: Tohoku earthquake & tsunami
desc: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck Japan, triggering a massive tsunami that killed over 18,000 people and caused the Fukushima nuclear disaster.

title: First female priest ordained
desc: The Church of England ordained its first 32 female priests at Bristol Cathedral, ending centuries of male-only priesthood.

title: Discovery of Uranus
desc: William Herschel discovered the planet Uranus, the first planet discovered with a telescope and the first new planet since antiquity.

title: Birth of Albert Einstein
desc: German-born physicist Albert Einstein, who developed the theory of relativity, was born in Ulm, Germany.

title: Death of Karl Marx
desc: German philosopher and economist Karl Marx, author of 'Das Kapital' and co-author of the 'Communist Manifesto', died in London.

title: Death of Stephen Hawking
desc: British theoretical physicist Stephen Hawking died at his home in Cambridge, aged 76, exactly 139 years after Einstein's birth.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
desc: Roman dictator Julius Caesar was stabbed to death by senators led by Brutus and Cassius on the Ides of March.

title: First liquid-fuel rocket
desc: American physicist Robert Goddard launched the world's first liquid-fueled rocket in Auburn, Massachusetts.

title: First spacewalk
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov became the first person to walk in space, leaving his Voskhod 2 capsule for 12 minutes.

title: Death of Isaac Newton
desc: English mathematician and physicist Sir Isaac Newton, who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation, died in London.

title: Sharpeville massacre
desc: South African police killed 69 peaceful anti-apartheid protesters in Sharpeville, drawing global condemnation.

title: First movie projected
desc: Auguste and Louis Lumiere gave the first public film screening in Paris, marking the birth of cinema.

title: Exxon Valdez oil spill
desc: The tanker Exxon Valdez struck a reef in Alaska's Prince William Sound, spilling 11 million gallons of crude oil.

title: Treaty of Rome signed
desc: The Treaty establishing the European Economic Community was signed in Rome by six nations, the foundation of today's European Union.

title: Death of Beethoven
desc: German composer Ludwig van Beethoven died in Vienna, aged 56, having completed his Ninth Symphony while completely deaf.

title: Death of Yuri Gagarin
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space, died in a MiG-15 fighter jet crash near Moscow, aged 34.

title: Three Mile Island accident
desc: A partial nuclear meltdown occurred at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station in Pennsylvania, the worst U.S. nuclear accident.

title: Birth of Vincent van Gogh
desc: Dutch post-impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh, whose work had enormous influence on 20th-century art, was born in Zundert.

title: Death of Charlotte Bronte
desc: English novelist Charlotte Bronte, author of 'Jane Eyre', died in Haworth, Yorkshire, aged 38, during pregnancy.

title: Eiffel Tower inaugurated
desc: The Eiffel Tower was officially inaugurated in Paris during the World's Fair celebrating the French Revolution centennial.

title: Apple founded
desc: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer Company in Cupertino, California.

title: Death of Pope John Paul II
desc: Pope John Paul II died at age 84 after a 26-year papacy, the second-longest in modern history.

title: First mobile phone call
desc: Motorola's Martin Cooper made the first handheld cellular phone call on a New York City street.

title: Assassination of MLK
desc: Civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee.

title: Death of Kurt Cobain
desc: Nirvana frontman Kurt Cobain was found dead in his Seattle home from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

title: First modern Olympics
desc: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece, with 280 athletes from 13 nations competing.

title: North Pole claimed
desc: American explorer Robert Peary claimed to have reached the North Pole, though the claim remains disputed.

title: WHO founded
desc: The World Health Organization was established as a specialized agency of the United Nations.

title: Death of Picasso
desc: Spanish painter Pablo Picasso died in Mougins, France, aged 91.

title: Lee surrenders at Appomattox
desc: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Union General Ulysses S. Grant, effectively ending the American Civil War.

title: Eruption of Tambora
desc: Mount Tambora in Indonesia began one of the most powerful volcanic eruptions in recorded history, killing over 70,000 people.

title: Titanic sets sail
desc: The RMS Titanic departed Southampton on its maiden voyage, which would end in disaster five days later.

title: First human in space
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to orbit the Earth aboard Vostok 1, lasting 108 minutes.

title: First Space Shuttle launch
desc: Space Shuttle Columbia launched on STS-1, the first flight of the Space Shuttle program, with John Young and Robert Crippen.

title: Apollo 13 oxygen tank
desc: An oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13, aborting the Moon mission and forcing a dramatic rescue around the Moon.

title: Lincoln assassinated
desc: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C.; he died the next morning.

title: Birth of Leonardo da Vinci
desc: Italian Renaissance polymath Leonardo da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, was born in Vinci, Tuscany.

title: Titanic sinks
desc: The RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic after striking an iceberg, killing over 1,500 of the 2,200 people aboard.

title: Jackie Robinson breaks color barrier
desc: Jackie Robinson became the first African-American player in modern Major League Baseball, debuting for the Brooklyn Dodgers.

title: Hillsborough disaster
desc: 96 Liverpool fans were crushed to death at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield, England's worst sporting disaster.

title: Death of Albert Einstein
desc: Physicist Albert Einstein died in Princeton, New Jersey, aged 76, having revolutionized our understanding of space, time, and gravity.

title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
desc: The first military engagements of the American Revolutionary War took place in Massachusetts.

title: Birth of Adolf Hitler
desc: Adolf Hitler, the dictator who led Nazi Germany into World War II and orchestrated the Holocaust, was born in Braunau am Inn, Austria.

title: Pierre & Marie Curie isolate radium
desc: Pierre and Marie Curie successfully isolated the radioactive element radium, the culmination of years of work on pitchblende.

title: Founding of Rome
desc: According to tradition, Romulus founded the city of Rome on the Palatine Hill.

title: Death of Mark Twain
desc: American author Mark Twain, born Samuel Clemens, died in Redding, Connecticut, aged 74.

title: First Earth Day
desc: The first Earth Day was celebrated in the United States, marking the birth of the modern environmental movement.

title: Birth of Shakespeare
desc: English playwright and poet William Shakespeare, widely regarded as the greatest writer in English literature, was born in Stratford-upon-Avon.

title: Death of Shakespeare
desc: William Shakespeare died on his 52nd birthday in Stratford-upon-Avon, leaving behind 39 plays and 154 sonnets.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
desc: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched aboard Space Shuttle Discovery, revolutionizing astronomy for the next three decades.

title: DNA structure published
desc: James Watson and Francis Crick's paper on the double-helix structure of DNA was published in the journal Nature.

title: Chernobyl disaster
desc: Reactor No. 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant exploded in Soviet Ukraine, the worst nuclear accident in history.

title: Death of Mussolini
desc: Italian fascist dictator Benito Mussolini was executed by Italian partisans and his body hung upside down in Milan.

title: Washington inaugurated
desc: George Washington was inaugurated as the first President of the United States at Federal Hall in New York City.

title: Hitler's suicide
desc: Adolf Hitler committed suicide in his Berlin bunker, ending his 12-year dictatorship of Nazi Germany.

title: Act of Union signed
desc: The Act of Union united England and Scotland into the Kingdom of Great Britain, taking effect on May 1.

title: Empire State Building opens
desc: The Empire State Building was officially opened in New York City, then the tallest building in the world.

title: Death of Napoleon
desc: French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte died in British exile on the island of St. Helena in the South Atlantic, aged 51.

title: Hindenburg disaster
desc: The German airship Hindenburg burst into flames while landing in New Jersey, killing 36 and ending the era of passenger airships.

title: Birth of Tchaikovsky
desc: Russian composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was born in Votkinsk, Russia.

title: Germany surrenders
desc: Nazi Germany signed an unconditional surrender at Allied headquarters in Reims, France, ending the war in Europe.

title: Coca-Cola invented
desc: Pharmacist John Pemberton first sold Coca-Cola at Jacobs' Pharmacy in Atlanta, Georgia.

title: VE Day
desc: Victory in Europe Day was celebrated as the end of World War II in Europe was formally accepted by the Allies.

title: Mandela inaugurated
desc: Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as President of South Africa, the country's first black head of state.

title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
desc: IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer to defeat a reigning world chess champion in a match, beating Garry Kasparov 3.5-2.5.

title: First smallpox vaccination
desc: English doctor Edward Jenner tested the first smallpox vaccine on 8-year-old James Phipps, using cowpox.

title: Israel established
desc: The State of Israel was declared by David Ben-Gurion, immediately leading to war with neighboring Arab states.

title: First airline stewardess
desc: Ellen Church became the world's first airline stewardess, working a Boeing Air Transport flight from Oakland to Chicago.

title: NY Stock Exchange founded
desc: 24 brokers signed the Buttonwood Agreement under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street, founding the New York Stock Exchange.

title: Mount St. Helens erupts
desc: Mount St. Helens in Washington state erupted in a massive explosion, killing 57 people and reducing the mountain's height by 1,300 feet.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
desc: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama became the first European to reach India by sea, arriving at Calicut after sailing around Africa.

title: Lindbergh takes off
desc: American aviator Charles Lindbergh took off from New York in the Spirit of St. Louis on the first solo non-stop transatlantic flight.

title: Lindbergh reaches Paris
desc: Charles Lindbergh landed at Le Bourget Field near Paris, completing the first solo non-stop transatlantic airplane flight in 33.5 hours.

title: Death of Victor Hugo
desc: French novelist and poet Victor Hugo, author of 'Les Miserables' and 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame', died in Paris.

title: Bonnie & Clyde killed
desc: Outlaws Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were shot and killed in an ambush by law officers in Bienville Parish, Louisiana.

title: First Morse telegraph message
desc: Samuel Morse sent the first telegraph message 'What hath God wrought' from Washington D.C. to Baltimore.

title: JFK Moon speech
desc: President John F. Kennedy announced the goal of landing a man on the Moon before the end of the decade.

title: 'Star Wars' released
desc: George Lucas's 'Star Wars' opened in U.S. theaters, becoming one of the highest-grossing and most influential films in history.

title: First Dow Jones published
desc: The Wall Street Journal first published the Dow Jones Industrial Average, then composed of 12 industrial stocks.

title: Fall of Constantinople
desc: Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire after 1,000 years.

title: Execution of Joan of Arc
desc: French heroine Joan of Arc was burned at the stake in Rouen, France, by the English at age 19.

title: Death of Haydn
desc: Austrian composer Joseph Haydn died in Vienna, aged 77.

title: First Scotch whisky record
desc: The first written record of Scotch whisky appeared in the Exchequer Rolls of Scotland, in the accounts of Friar John Cor.

title: Death of Helen Keller
desc: American author and activist Helen Keller died in Easton, Connecticut, aged 87.

title: First American spacewalk
desc: Astronaut Ed White became the first American to walk in space during the Gemini 4 mission.

title: First hot-air balloon flight
desc: The Montgolfier brothers demonstrated their hot-air balloon with the first unmanned flight in Annonay, France.

title: Marshall Plan announced
desc: U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall announced the European Recovery Program to rebuild Western Europe after WWII.

title: Assassination of RFK
desc: U.S. Senator and presidential candidate Robert F. Kennedy was shot in Los Angeles, dying the next day.

title: D-Day landings
desc: Allied forces launched the Normandy landings (D-Day), the largest seaborne invasion in history, beginning the liberation of Western Europe.

title: Death of Prophet Muhammad
desc: Muhammad, the founder of Islam, died in Medina after a brief illness, having unified the Arabian Peninsula.

title: Death of Charles Dickens
desc: English novelist Charles Dickens died at Gad's Hill Place, Kent, aged 58, after a stroke.

title: AA founded
desc: Alcoholics Anonymous was founded in Akron, Ohio, by Bill Wilson and Dr. Bob Smith, launching a global recovery movement.

title: Philippines independence declared
desc: The Philippines declared independence from Spain, though it would not gain true independence until 1946.

title: Death of Alexander the Great
desc: Alexander the Great, who created one of the largest empires in history by age 30, died in Babylon at age 32.

title: Hawaii becomes U.S. territory
desc: The Hawaiian Islands became a U.S. territory, after the overthrow of the Hawaiian monarchy in 1893.

title: Birth of Che Guevara
desc: Argentine Marxist revolutionary Ernesto 'Che' Guevara was born in Rosario, Argentina.

title: Magna Carta signed
desc: King John of England sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede, establishing key principles of limited government and rule of law.

title: Franklin's kite experiment
desc: Benjamin Franklin flew a kite in a thunderstorm, demonstrating that lightning is electricity.

title: First woman in space
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space aboard Vostok 6, orbiting Earth 48 times.

title: Battle of Waterloo
desc: An allied army led by Wellington and Prussian forces defeated Napoleon Bonaparte at Waterloo, ending his rule.

title: Victoria becomes queen
desc: Alexandrina Victoria became Queen of the United Kingdom at age 18, beginning a 63-year reign.

title: First stored-program computer
desc: The Manchester Small-Scale Experimental Machine (the 'Baby') ran its first program, the world's first stored-program computer.

title: Birth of Alan Turing
desc: British mathematician Alan Turing, father of theoretical computer science and AI, was born in London.

title: Reddit founded
desc: Social news platform Reddit was founded by Steve Huffman and Alexis Ohanian in Medford, Massachusetts.

title: UK Brexit vote
desc: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, 52% to 48%, in a historic referendum.

title: Cabot reaches North America
desc: Italian explorer John Cabot, sailing for England, landed in North America, likely in Newfoundland, Canada.

title: Battle of Little Bighorn
desc: A combined force of Lakota and Northern Cheyenne warriors defeated the U.S. 7th Cavalry under Custer in Montana.

title: UN Charter signed
desc: Representatives of 50 nations signed the United Nations Charter in San Francisco, establishing the UN.

title: Birth of Helen Keller
desc: American author and activist Helen Keller, deaf and blind from age 19 months, was born in Tuscumbia, Alabama.

title: Assassination of Franz Ferdinand
desc: Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip, triggering World War I.

title: Treaty of Versailles
desc: The Treaty of Versailles was signed, officially ending World War I and imposing harsh terms on Germany.

title: Tunguska event
desc: A massive explosion, likely caused by a meteor airburst, flattened 80 million trees over 2,000 sq km in remote Siberia.

title: First TV commercial
desc: The first legal television commercial aired in the U.S. on WNBT before a Brooklyn Dodgers game.

title: Hong Kong handover
desc: The United Kingdom transferred sovereignty of Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China after 156 years of British rule.

title: Death of Rousseau
desc: Philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau died in Ermenonville, France, aged 66.

title: Garfield shot
desc: U.S. President James A. Garfield was shot at a Washington train station by Charles Guiteau, dying 79 days later.

title: Death of Hemingway
desc: American novelist Ernest Hemingway died by suicide at his home in Ketchum, Idaho, aged 61.

title: U.S. Declaration of Independence
desc: The United States declared independence from Great Britain, adopted by the Continental Congress in Philadelphia.

title: Death of Marie Curie
desc: Marie Curie died in France from aplastic anemia, caused by her radiation research, aged 66.

title: U.S. Bicentennial
desc: The United States celebrated its 200th anniversary of independence with nationwide festivities.

title: Amazon founded
desc: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon.com in Seattle, initially as an online bookstore, later becoming the world's largest online retailer.

title: First rabies vaccine
desc: Louis Pasteur successfully tested his rabies vaccine on 9-year-old Joseph Meister, who had been bitten by a rabid dog.

title: Birth of Ringo Starr
desc: Beatles drummer Ringo Starr (born Richard Starkey) was born in Liverpool, England.

title: Death of Jim Morrison
desc: Doors frontman Jim Morrison was found dead in his Paris apartment bathtub, aged 27, of heart failure.

title: Birth of Nikola Tesla
desc: Serbian-American inventor Nikola Tesla, pioneer of alternating current electricity, was born in Smiljan, Austrian Empire.

title: First communications satellite
desc: Telstar, the first active communications satellite, was launched, enabling the first transatlantic television transmissions.

title: Storming of the Bastille
desc: Parisians stormed the Bastille prison, the flashpoint of the French Revolution, now celebrated as France's national day.

title: Twitter launches
desc: Twitter (later X) was launched, becoming a major social media platform for real-time communication.

title: Trinity nuclear test
desc: The United States successfully detonated the world's first atomic bomb in the New Mexico desert, beginning the nuclear age.

title: Apollo 11 launches
desc: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center carrying Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins on the first Moon landing mission.

title: Disneyland opens
desc: Walt Disney's Disneyland theme park opened in Anaheim, California, the first of its kind.

title: Apollo-Soyuz docking
desc: U.S. Apollo and Soviet Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, the first international space collaboration and symbolic end of the Space Race.

title: Birth of Nelson Mandela
desc: Nelson Mandela, anti-apartheid revolutionary and first black President of South Africa, was born in Mvezo, South Africa.

title: First Tour de France
desc: Maurice Garin won the first Tour de France cycling race, covering 2,428 km in 19 days.

title: First Moon landing
desc: Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon, declaring 'that's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

title: Birth of Hemingway
desc: American novelist Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois.

title: Comet Hale-Bopp discovered
desc: Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp independently discovered Comet Hale-Bopp, one of the brightest comets of the 20th century.

title: Apollo 11 returns
desc: Apollo 11 and its three astronauts splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean, completing the first crewed Moon landing mission.

title: First test-tube baby
desc: Louise Brown, the world's first baby conceived via in vitro fertilization (IVF), was born in Oldham, England.

title: Birth of Mick Jagger
desc: British rock singer Mick Jagger, frontman of the Rolling Stones, was born in Dartford, Kent, England.

title: Death of J.S. Bach
desc: German composer Johann Sebastian Bach died in Leipzig, aged 65, leaving a vast musical legacy.

title: WWI begins
desc: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, beginning World War I, exactly one month after Franz Ferdinand's assassination.

title: Tangshan earthquake
desc: A massive 7.8 earthquake struck Tangshan, China, killing an estimated 242,000 people, one of the deadliest in history.

title: NASA founded
desc: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) was established by U.S. President Eisenhower.

title: Charles & Diana wedding
desc: Prince Charles married Lady Diana Spencer at St Paul's Cathedral in London, watched by 750 million people worldwide.

title: First World Cup final
desc: Uruguay won the first FIFA World Cup, defeating Argentina 4-2 in the final in Montevideo.

title: 1966 World Cup final
desc: England won their only FIFA World Cup, beating West Germany 4-2 at Wembley Stadium, with Geoff Hurst's hat-trick.

title: MTV launches
desc: Music television channel MTV launched with the words 'Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll' and the Buggles' 'Video Killed the Radio Star'.

title: Iraq invades Kuwait
desc: Iraq under Saddam Hussein invaded neighboring Kuwait, triggering the Gulf War and a U.S.-led international response.

title: Columbus departs
desc: Christopher Columbus set sail from Palos, Spain, on his first voyage to find a western route to Asia.

title: Birth of Neil Armstrong
desc: American astronaut Neil Armstrong, the first human to walk on the Moon, was born in Wapakoneta, Ohio.

title: Hiroshima atomic bomb
desc: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan, killing an estimated 140,000 people by the end of the year.

title: First website
desc: Tim Berners-Lee posted the first website at CERN, describing the World Wide Web project.

title: Nagasaki atomic bomb
desc: The United States dropped a second atomic bomb on Nagasaki, Japan, killing an estimated 70,000 people.

title: IBM PC released
desc: IBM released the IBM Personal Computer (model 5150), the machine that established the PC standard for decades.

title: Berlin Wall built
desc: East Germany began constructing the Berlin Wall, sealing off East Berlin from West Berlin for 28 years.

title: V-J Day
desc: Japan surrendered unconditionally to the Allies, effectively ending World War II (formal signing came September 2).

title: Woodstock festival begins
desc: The Woodstock Music and Art Fair opened in Bethel, New York, becoming the defining event of the 1960s counterculture.

title: Death of Elvis Presley
desc: Elvis Presley, the 'King of Rock and Roll', died at his Graceland home in Memphis, Tennessee, aged 42.

title: Death of Augustus
desc: Augustus, the first Roman Emperor, died at age 75 after a 41-year reign that began the Roman Principate.

title: Mona Lisa stolen
desc: Vincenzo Peruggia stole Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa from the Louvre; it was recovered in Florence in 1913.

title: Hawaii becomes 50th state
desc: Hawaii became the 50th and most recent state of the United States of America.

title: Eruption of Vesuvius
desc: Mount Vesuvius erupted, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum and killing thousands.

title: Sack of Rome by Visigoths
desc: Visigoths under Alaric sacked Rome for the first time in 800 years, shocking the Roman world.

title: Galileo demonstrates telescope
desc: Galileo Galilei demonstrated his telescope to the Venetian Senate, opening a new era of astronomical observation.

title: Birth of Leonard Bernstein
desc: American composer and conductor Leonard Bernstein was born in Lawrence, Massachusetts.

title: Death of Neil Armstrong
desc: Astronaut Neil Armstrong died in Cincinnati, Ohio, aged 82, three weeks after heart surgery.

title: Eruption of Krakatoa
desc: The volcanic island of Krakatoa in Indonesia erupted in a catastrophic explosion heard 3,000 miles away, killing over 36,000.

title: 'I Have a Dream' speech
desc: Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his iconic 'I Have a Dream' speech at the Lincoln Memorial during the March on Washington.

title: Birth of Michael Jackson
desc: Pop superstar Michael Jackson was born in Gary, Indiana, the seventh of nine Jackson children.

title: Netflix founded
desc: Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph founded Netflix in Scotts Valley, California, initially as a DVD rental-by-mail service.

title: Death of Cleopatra
desc: Egyptian queen Cleopatra VII died in Alexandria, traditionally by snakebite, ending the Ptolemaic dynasty.

title: Death of Princess Diana
desc: Diana, Princess of Wales, was killed in a car crash in Paris, aged 36, along with Dodi Fayed and driver Henri Paul.

title: Great Kanto earthquake
desc: A 7.9 earthquake struck the Kanto region of Japan, killing over 100,000 people and destroying Tokyo and Yokohama.

title: WWII begins
desc: Nazi Germany invaded Poland, prompting Britain and France to declare war two days later, beginning World War II.

title: Great Fire of London
desc: A major fire swept through central London for four days, destroying around 13,200 houses and 87 churches including St Paul's.

title: Japan formally surrenders
desc: Japan signed the formal surrender documents aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, officially ending World War II.

title: Munich massacre
desc: Palestinian terrorists killed 11 Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympics, shocking the world live on television.

title: Voyager 1 launched
desc: NASA launched Voyager 1, now the most distant human-made object, heading into interstellar space.

title: McKinley shot
desc: U.S. President William McKinley was shot by anarchist Leon Czolgosz in Buffalo, NY, dying on September 14.

title: Birth of Elizabeth I
desc: Queen Elizabeth I of England, who would rule during the Elizabethan era, was born at Greenwich Palace.

title: Death of William the Conqueror
desc: William I, the Norman King of England who invaded in 1066, died in Rouen, France, after a fall from his horse.

title: First computer bug
desc: Operators of the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth causing a malfunction, the first literal 'computer bug'.

title: LHC first beam
desc: CERN's Large Hadron Collider, the world's largest particle accelerator, was first put into operation beneath Switzerland.

title: September 11 attacks
desc: Terrorists hijacked four airliners, crashing two into the World Trade Center and one into the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people.

title: JFK Moon speech at Rice
desc: President Kennedy declared 'we choose to go to the Moon' in his speech at Rice University.

title: Death of Tupac Shakur
desc: American rapper Tupac Shakur died in Las Vegas, six days after being shot in a drive-by shooting, aged 25.

title: Birth of Amy Winehouse
desc: British singer Amy Winehouse was born in Southgate, London.

title: Liverpool & Manchester Railway
desc: The world's first inter-city passenger railway opened in England, marking the dawn of the railway age.

title: Mayflower departs
desc: The Mayflower set sail from Plymouth, England, carrying Pilgrims who would found Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts.

title: US Constitution signed
desc: The U.S. Constitution was signed in Philadelphia, replacing the Articles of Confederation.

title: Death of Jimi Hendrix
desc: Guitarist Jimi Hendrix died in London, aged 27, from asphyxia after taking sleeping pills.

title: Death of James Garfield
desc: U.S. President James A. Garfield died from wounds after being shot by an assassin on July 2.

title: Magellan's voyage begins
desc: Ferdinand Magellan set sail from Spain with five ships on the first circumnavigation of the globe.

title: Lincoln's Emancipation preview
desc: President Lincoln issued the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation, warning the Confederacy of emancipation to come.

title: Discovery of Neptune
desc: German astronomer Johann Galle discovered Neptune based on mathematical predictions by Le Verrier.

title: Death of Sigmund Freud
desc: Sigmund Freud died in London by physician-assisted morphine overdose, aged 83, fleeing Nazi Austria.

title: First transatlantic telephone cable
desc: TAT-1, the first transatlantic telephone cable, went into service between Scotland and Newfoundland.

title: Soviet nuclear false alarm
desc: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov correctly judged a U.S. missile launch warning as false, likely preventing nuclear war.

title: Taliban take Kabul
desc: The Taliban captured Afghanistan's capital Kabul, beginning five years of strict Islamist rule.

title: Penicillin discovered
desc: Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold (Penicillium) had killed bacteria in a petri dish, leading to the first antibiotic.

title: First shuttle post-Challenger
desc: Space Shuttle Discovery launched on STS-26, the first shuttle mission after the Challenger disaster.

title: PRC founded
desc: Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.

title: Birth of Mahatma Gandhi
desc: Mohandas K. Gandhi, leader of India's independence movement, was born in Porbandar, India.

title: Sputnik 1 launched
desc: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, starting the Space Age and the Space Race.

title: Instagram launches
desc: Photo-sharing app Instagram was launched by Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger, later acquired by Facebook for $1 billion.

title: Spotify launches
desc: Music streaming service Spotify launched in Europe, transforming how the world listens to music.

title: Birth of John Lennon
desc: Beatles member and solo artist John Lennon was born in Liverpool, England.

title: Death of Che Guevara
desc: Argentine revolutionary Che Guevara was executed by Bolivian forces after his capture in the Bolivian jungle.

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
desc: Christopher Columbus made landfall in the Bahamas, opening the way for European colonization of the Americas.

title: Death of Claudius
desc: Roman Emperor Claudius died in Rome, reportedly poisoned by his wife Agrippina; Nero succeeded him.

title: Battle of Hastings
desc: William, Duke of Normandy defeated King Harold II of England, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

title: First supersonic flight
desc: American test pilot Chuck Yeager became the first person to break the sound barrier, flying the Bell X-1.

title: Death of Bernstein
desc: American conductor and composer Leonard Bernstein died in New York, aged 72.

title: Birth of Nietzsche
desc: German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche was born in Rocken, Prussia.

title: Execution of Marie Antoinette
desc: Marie Antoinette, Queen of France, was guillotined during the French Revolution's Reign of Terror.

title: Death of Chopin
desc: Polish composer Frederic Chopin died in Paris, aged 39, of tuberculosis.

title: Death of Thomas Edison
desc: American inventor Thomas Edison died at his West Orange, New Jersey laboratory, aged 84, holder of 1,093 U.S. patents.

title: Yorktown surrender
desc: British General Cornwallis surrendered to George Washington at Yorktown, effectively ending the American Revolution.

title: Birth of Alfred Nobel
desc: Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, who invented dynamite and founded the Nobel Prizes, was born in Stockholm.

title: Edison's light bulb
desc: Thomas Edison successfully tested the first practical incandescent light bulb, which burned for over 13 hours.

title: First parachute jump
desc: Frenchman Andre-Jacques Garnerin made the first parachute descent from a balloon 3,200 feet above Paris.

title: First iPod released
desc: Apple CEO Steve Jobs introduced the iPod, with '1,000 songs in your pocket', transforming the music industry.

title: United Nations founded
desc: The United Nations officially came into existence, with the UN Charter ratified by the five permanent Security Council members.

title: Charge of the Light Brigade
desc: A miscommunicated order sent British light cavalry into Russian artillery during the Crimean War's Battle of Balaclava.

title: Birth of Niccolo Paganini
desc: Italian violin virtuoso Niccolo Paganini was born in Genoa.

title: Death of John Locke
desc: English philosopher John Locke died at Oates, Essex, aged 72.

title: Statue of Liberty dedicated
desc: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, was dedicated in New York Harbor by President Grover Cleveland.

title: Birth of Bill Gates
desc: Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates was born in Seattle, Washington.

title: Black Tuesday
desc: The U.S. stock market crashed, with the Dow Jones falling 12%, marking the start of the Great Depression.

title: First Internet message
desc: The first message was sent over ARPANET, the predecessor of the Internet, from UCLA to Stanford.

title: Sistine Chapel ceiling
desc: Michelangelo's painted ceiling of the Sistine Chapel was first shown to the public by Pope Julius II.

title: Gunpowder Plot foiled
desc: Guy Fawkes was caught guarding explosives beneath the House of Lords in a failed Catholic plot to kill King James I.

title: Birth of Marie Curie
desc: Polish-French physicist and chemist Marie Curie, the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, was born in Warsaw.

title: October Revolution
desc: Bolsheviks led by Vladimir Lenin seized power in Petrograd, leading to the creation of the Soviet Union.

title: X-rays discovered
desc: German physicist Wilhelm Rontgen discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode rays, revolutionizing medicine.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
desc: East Germany unexpectedly opened its borders, and Berliners began tearing down the Wall that had divided the city for 28 years.

title: End of WWI
desc: An armistice was signed at 11 a.m. in a railway carriage in Compiegne Forest, ending World War I.

title: Elizabeth I accession
desc: Elizabeth I became Queen of England following the death of her half-sister Mary I, beginning the Elizabethan era.

title: Gettysburg Address
desc: President Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at the dedication of the military cemetery at Gettysburg.

title: Nuremberg trials begin
desc: The Nuremberg trials of 22 leading Nazi officials began in Nuremberg, Germany, for crimes against humanity.

title: First hot-air balloon manned flight
desc: Jean-Francois Pilatre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes made the first manned free balloon flight in Paris.

title: Assassination of JFK
desc: U.S. President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas, Texas, by Lee Harvey Oswald, shocking the world.

title: 'Origin of Species' published
desc: Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' was published, introducing the theory of evolution by natural selection.

title: Tutankhamun tomb opened
desc: Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon became the first people to enter Tutankhamun's tomb in over 3,000 years.

title: First Harry Potter published
desc: J.K. Rowling's 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' was published, launching the best-selling book series in history.

title: Birth of Mark Twain
desc: American author Mark Twain, born Samuel Clemens, was born in Florida, Missouri.

title: Death of Oscar Wilde
desc: Irish playwright and wit Oscar Wilde, author of 'The Importance of Being Earnest', died in Paris, aged 46.

title: ChatGPT launched
desc: OpenAI launched ChatGPT, becoming the fastest-growing consumer application in history with 100M users in 2 months.

title: Rosa Parks arrested
desc: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white man, sparking the bus boycott.

title: First heart transplant
desc: South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant in Cape Town.

title: Death of Mozart
desc: Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart died in Vienna, aged 35, leaving his Requiem unfinished.

title: Birth of Walt Disney
desc: American animator and entrepreneur Walter Elias Disney, who founded the Disney empire, was born in Chicago.

title: Death of Nelson Mandela
desc: Nelson Mandela died in Johannesburg, aged 95, after a life of fighting apartheid and uniting South Africa.

title: Pearl Harbor attacked
desc: Japan attacked the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, killing 2,400 Americans and bringing the U.S. into WWII.

title: Birth of Jim Morrison
desc: Doors frontman Jim Morrison was born in Melbourne, Florida.

title: Death of John Lennon
desc: Former Beatle John Lennon was shot and killed outside his New York apartment by Mark David Chapman.

title: Death of Alfred Nobel
desc: Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, who invented dynamite and established the Nobel Prizes, died in San Remo, Italy.

title: First Nobel Prizes
desc: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in Stockholm and Oslo on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.

title: OpenAI founded
desc: OpenAI was founded in San Francisco by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, and others, with a $1 billion pledge.

title: Edward VIII abdicates
desc: King Edward VIII abdicated the British throne to marry American divorcee Wallis Simpson, ending a 325-day reign.

title: South Pole reached
desc: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen became the first person to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Scott's party.

title: 'Gone with the Wind' premiere
desc: The film 'Gone with the Wind' premiered in Atlanta, Georgia, becoming one of the highest-grossing films of all time.

title: First airplane flight
desc: The Wright brothers made the first sustained, controlled, powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

title: 2022 World Cup final
desc: Argentina won the FIFA World Cup, beating France on penalties in one of the greatest finals ever, with Messi's hat-trick.

title: 'Titanic' released
desc: James Cameron's 'Titanic' was released in U.S. theaters, becoming the first film to gross $1 billion.

title: Pilgrims land at Plymouth
desc: The Mayflower Pilgrims landed at Plymouth Rock, Massachusetts, founding one of the first permanent European settlements in New England.

title: 'Snow White' premieres
desc: Walt Disney's 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs', the first full-length cel-animated feature film, premiered in Los Angeles.

title: Apollo 8 launches
desc: Apollo 8 became the first crewed mission to leave Earth orbit and orbit the Moon, broadcasting images of 'Earthrise'.

title: Transistor invented
desc: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley at Bell Labs demonstrated the first working transistor.

title: Birth of Isaac Newton
desc: English mathematician and physicist Sir Isaac Newton was born in Woolsthorpe, Lincolnshire (under the Julian calendar then in use in England).

title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns
desc: Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev resigned, and the Soviet Union was formally dissolved the next day.

title: James Webb Telescope launches
desc: The James Webb Space Telescope, successor to Hubble, was launched from French Guiana aboard an Ariane 5 rocket.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami
desc: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra triggered a tsunami that killed around 230,000 people across 14 countries.

title: Birth of Johannes Kepler
desc: German astronomer Johannes Kepler, who formulated the laws of planetary motion, was born in Weil der Stadt.

title: HMS Beagle departs
desc: Charles Darwin set sail aboard HMS Beagle on a five-year voyage that would inspire his theory of evolution.

title: Death of Pele
desc: Brazilian football legend Pele died in Sao Paulo, aged 82, from colon cancer.

title: Death of Grigori Rasputin
desc: Russian mystic Grigori Rasputin was killed by Russian nobles in Petrograd after surviving poison and gunshot wounds.

title: Y2K panic
desc: The world prepared for the Y2K computer bug as the year 2000 approached; major disruptions were largely averted.
